nodes.Name: explode
nodes.DocComment:
explode splits s into a slice of UTF-8 strings,
one string per Unicode character up to a maximum of n (n < 0 means no limit).
Invalid UTF-8 bytes are sliced individually.

nodes.Name: Count
nodes.DocComment:
Count counts the number of non-overlapping instances of substr in s.
If substr is an empty string, Count returns 1 + the number of Unicode code points in s.

nodes.Name: Contains
nodes.DocComment: Contains reports whether substr is within s.

nodes.Name: ContainsAny
nodes.DocComment: ContainsAny reports whether any Unicode code points in chars are within s.

nodes.Name: ContainsRune
nodes.DocComment: ContainsRune reports whether the Unicode code point r is within s.

nodes.Name: ContainsFunc
nodes.DocComment: ContainsFunc reports whether any Unicode code points r within s satisfy f(r).

nodes.Name: LastIndex
nodes.DocComment: LastIndex returns the index of the last instance of substr in s, or -1 if substr is not present in s.

nodes.Name: IndexByte
nodes.DocComment: IndexByte returns the index of the first instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

nodes.Name: IndexRune
nodes.DocComment:
IndexRune returns the index of the first instance of the Unicode code point
r, or -1 if rune is not present in s.
If r is [utf8.RuneError], it returns the first instance of any
invalid UTF-8 byte sequence.

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: (haveFastIndex && fails > bytealg.Cutover(i)) && i < len(s) || (!haveFastIndex && fails >= 4+i>>4 && i < len(s))

nodes.Name: IndexAny
nodes.DocComment:
IndexAny returns the index of the first instance of any Unicode code point
from chars in s, or -1 if no Unicode code point from chars is present in s.

nodes.Name: LastIndexAny
nodes.DocComment:
LastIndexAny returns the index of the last instance of any Unicode code
point from chars in s, or -1 if no Unicode code point from chars is
present in s.

nodes.Name: LastIndexByte
nodes.DocComment: LastIndexByte returns the index of the last instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

nodes.Name: genSplit
nodes.DocComment:
Generic split: splits after each instance of sep,
including sepSave bytes of sep in the subarrays.

nodes.Name: SplitN
nodes.DocComment:
SplitN slices s into substrings separated by sep and returns a slice of
the substrings between those separators.

The count determines the number of substrings to return:
  - n > 0: at most n substrings; the last substring will be the unsplit remainder;
  - n == 0: the result is nil (zero substrings);
  - n < 0: all substrings.

Edge cases for s and sep (for example, empty strings) are handled
as described in the documentation for [Split].

To split around the first instance of a separator, see [Cut].

nodes.Name: SplitAfterN
nodes.DocComment:
SplitAfterN slices s into substrings after each instance of sep and
returns a slice of those substrings.

The count determines the number of substrings to return:
  - n > 0: at most n substrings; the last substring will be the unsplit remainder;
  - n == 0: the result is nil (zero substrings);
  - n < 0: all substrings.

Edge cases for s and sep (for example, empty strings) are handled
as described in the documentation for [SplitAfter].

nodes.Name: Split
nodes.DocComment:
Split slices s into all substrings separated by sep and returns a slice of
the substrings between those separators.

If s does not contain sep and sep is not empty, Split returns a
slice of length 1 whose only element is s.

If sep is empty, Split splits after each UTF-8 sequence. If both s
and sep are empty, Split returns an empty slice.

It is equivalent to [SplitN] with a count of -1.

To split around the first instance of a separator, see [Cut].

nodes.Name: SplitAfter
nodes.DocComment:
SplitAfter slices s into all substrings after each instance of sep and
returns a slice of those substrings.

If s does not contain sep and sep is not empty, SplitAfter returns
a slice of length 1 whose only element is s.

If sep is empty, SplitAfter splits after each UTF-8 sequence. If
both s and sep are empty, SplitAfter returns an empty slice.

It is equivalent to [SplitAfterN] with a count of -1.

nodes.Name: Fields
nodes.DocComment:
Fields splits the string s around each instance of one or more consecutive white space
characters, as defined by [unicode.IsSpace], returning a slice of substrings of s or an
empty slice if s contains only white space. Every element of the returned slice is
non-empty. Unlike [Split], leading and trailing runs runs of white space characters
are discarded.

nodes.Name: FieldsFunc
nodes.DocComment:
FieldsFunc splits the string s at each run of Unicode code points c satisfying f(c)
and returns an array of slices of s. If all code points in s satisfy f(c) or the
string is empty, an empty slice is returned. Every element of the returned slice is
non-empty. Unlike [SplitFunc], leading and trailing runs of code points satisfying f(c)
are discarded.

FieldsFunc makes no guarantees about the order in which it calls f(c)
and assumes that f always returns the same value for a given c.

nodes.Name: Join
nodes.DocComment:
Join concatenates the elements of its first argument to create a single string. The separator
string sep is placed between elements in the resulting string.

nodes.Name: HasPrefix
nodes.DocComment: HasPrefix reports whether the string s begins with prefix.

nodes.Name: HasSuffix
nodes.DocComment: HasSuffix reports whether the string s ends with suffix.

nodes.Name: Map
nodes.DocComment:
Map returns a copy of the string s with all its characters modified
according to the mapping function. If mapping returns a negative value, the character is
dropped from the string with no replacement.

nodes.Name: repeatedSpaces
nodes.DocComment:
According to static analysis, spaces, dashes, zeros, equals, and tabs
are the most commonly repeated string literal,
often used for display on fixed-width terminal windows.
Pre-declare constants for these for O(1) repetition in the common-case.

nodes.DocComment:

nodes.Name: Repeat
nodes.DocComment:
Repeat returns a new string consisting of count copies of the string s.

It panics if count is negative or if the result of (len(s) * count)
overflows.

nodes.Name: ToUpper
nodes.DocComment: ToUpper returns s with all Unicode letters mapped to their upper case.

nodes.Name: ToLower
nodes.DocComment: ToLower returns s with all Unicode letters mapped to their lower case.

nodes.Name: ToTitle
nodes.DocComment:
ToTitle returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to
their Unicode title case.

nodes.Name: ToUpperSpecial
nodes.DocComment:
ToUpperSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their
upper case using the case mapping specified by c.

nodes.Name: ToLowerSpecial
nodes.DocComment:
ToLowerSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their
lower case using the case mapping specified by c.

nodes.Name: ToTitleSpecial
nodes.DocComment:
ToTitleSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their
Unicode title case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

nodes.Name: ToValidUTF8
nodes.DocComment:
ToValidUTF8 returns a copy of the string s with each run of invalid UTF-8 byte sequences
replaced by the replacement string, which may be empty.

nodes.Name: isSeparator
nodes.DocComment:
isSeparator reports whether the rune could mark a word boundary.
TODO: update when package unicode captures more of the properties.

nodes.Name: Title
nodes.DocComment:
Title returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters that begin words
mapped to their Unicode title case.

Deprecated: The rule Title uses for word boundaries does not handle Unicode
punctuation properly. Use golang.org/x/text/cases instead.

nodes.Name: TrimLeftFunc
nodes.DocComment:
TrimLeftFunc returns a slice of the string s with all leading
Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

nodes.Name: TrimRightFunc
nodes.DocComment:
TrimRightFunc returns a slice of the string s with all trailing
Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

nodes.Name: TrimFunc
nodes.DocComment:
TrimFunc returns a slice of the string s with all leading
and trailing Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

nodes.Name: IndexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
IndexFunc returns the index into s of the first Unicode
code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

nodes.Name: LastIndexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
LastIndexFunc returns the index into s of the last
Unicode code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

nodes.Name: indexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
indexFunc is the same as IndexFunc except that if
truth==false, the sense of the predicate function is
inverted.

nodes.Name: lastIndexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
lastIndexFunc is the same as LastIndexFunc except that if
truth==false, the sense of the predicate function is
inverted.

nodes.Name: asciiSet
nodes.DocComment:
asciiSet is a 32-byte value, where each bit represents the presence of a
given ASCII character in the set. The 128-bits of the lower 16 bytes,
starting with the least-significant bit of the lowest word to the
most-significant bit of the highest word, map to the full range of all
128 ASCII characters. The 128-bits of the upper 16 bytes will be zeroed,
ensuring that any non-ASCII character will be reported as not in the set.
This allocates a total of 32 bytes even though the upper half
is unused to avoid bounds checks in asciiSet.contains.

nodes.Name: makeASCIISet
nodes.DocComment:
makeASCIISet creates a set of ASCII characters and reports whether all
characters in chars are ASCII.

nodes.Name: contains
nodes.DocComment: contains reports whether c is inside the set.

nodes.Name: Trim
nodes.DocComment:
Trim returns a slice of the string s with all leading and
trailing Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

nodes.Name: TrimLeft
nodes.DocComment:
TrimLeft returns a slice of the string s with all leading
Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

To remove a prefix, use [TrimPrefix] instead.

nodes.Name: TrimRight
nodes.DocComment:
TrimRight returns a slice of the string s, with all trailing
Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

To remove a suffix, use [TrimSuffix] instead.

nodes.Name: TrimSpace
nodes.DocComment:
TrimSpace returns a slice of the string s, with all leading
and trailing white space removed, as defined by Unicode.

nodes.Name: TrimPrefix
nodes.DocComment:
TrimPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string.
If s doesn't start with prefix, s is returned unchanged.

nodes.Name: TrimSuffix
nodes.DocComment:
TrimSuffix returns s without the provided trailing suffix string.
If s doesn't end with suffix, s is returned unchanged.

nodes.Name: Replace
nodes.DocComment:
Replace returns a copy of the string s with the first n
non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.
If old is empty, it matches at the beginning of the string
and after each UTF-8 sequence, yielding up to k+1 replacements
for a k-rune string.
If n < 0, there is no limit on the number of replacements.

nodes.Name: ReplaceAll
nodes.DocComment:
ReplaceAll returns a copy of the string s with all
non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.
If old is empty, it matches at the beginning of the string
and after each UTF-8 sequence, yielding up to k+1 replacements
for a k-rune string.

nodes.Name: EqualFold
nodes.DocComment:
EqualFold reports whether s and t, interpreted as UTF-8 strings,
are equal under simple Unicode case-folding, which is a more general
form of case-insensitivity.

nodes.Name: Index
nodes.DocComment: Index returns the index of the first instance of substr in s, or -1 if substr is not present in s.

nodes.Name: Cut
nodes.DocComment:
Cut slices s around the first instance of sep,
returning the text before and after sep.
The found result reports whether sep appears in s.
If sep does not appear in s, cut returns s, "", false.

nodes.Name: CutPrefix
nodes.DocComment:
CutPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string
and reports whether it found the prefix.
If s doesn't start with prefix, CutPrefix returns s, false.
If prefix is the empty string, CutPrefix returns s, true.

nodes.Name: CutSuffix
nodes.DocComment:
CutSuffix returns s without the provided ending suffix string
and reports whether it found the suffix.
If s doesn't end with suffix, CutSuffix returns s, false.
If suffix is the empty string, CutSuffix returns s, true.
